docs.t: What is a pink slip?
docs.q: What is a pink slip?
docs.a: A pink slip is the safety check most light vehicles need to renew their rego once they're more than five years old, counted from the compliance plate date. It checks things like tyres, brakes, steering and suspension, lights, windscreen and wipers, seatbelts, body and rust, and the exhaust. The report is valid for six months.

docs.t: Do I need a blue slip?
docs.q: Do I need a blue slip?
docs.a: You need a blue slip, a safety and identity check, when the rego ran out more than three months ago, the vehicle comes from interstate or overseas, it has no plates, or it's a written-off vehicle being registered again. The report is valid for 42 days.

docs.t: My check engine light is on
docs.q: My check engine light is on
docs.a: Check engine is an amber light: get it checked soon. If it stays on steadily, you can usually drive on gently and book it in soon. If it flashes, the engine may be misfiring badly: slow down, stop somewhere safe as soon as you can and call. General guidance only; your owner's manual has the details for your car.

docs.t: Bring it to Unit 4B: What's that light on your dash?
docs.a: Tap the one you can see. You'll get what it usually means, whether it's generally safe to keep driving, and who at Shine looks after it. Red usually means stop when it's safe, or act now. Amber usually means get it checked soon. How to read a warning light. Choose a light to see what it usually means. Amber light: get it checked soon. Check engine. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. The engine computer has found a fault. It can be small, like a loose fuel cap, or something that needs fixing, like a sensor or ignition problem. Can I keep driving? If it stays on steadily, you can usually drive on gently and book it in soon. If it flashes, the engine may be misfiring badly: slow down, stop somewhere safe as soon as you can and call, as driving on can damage the exhaust system. Your owner's manual has the details for your car. Who handles it at Shine. All mechanical repairs (engine). Red light: act now. Battery or charging. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. The battery isn't being charged. Common causes are a worn alternator, a loose or broken drive belt, or a battery or wiring fault. Can I keep driving? Not far. The car is running on what's left in the battery and may stop. Switch off what you don't need, like the air con and radio, and get somewhere safe. If other lights come on too, stop. Who handles it at Shine. Batteries, and all mechanical repairs for the charging system. Red light: stop safely. Oil pressure. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. Oil pressure is too low. The engine may be low on oil, or there may be a fault with the oil pump or a sensor. Can I keep driving? No. Stop as soon as it's safe and switch the engine off. An engine without oil pressure can be damaged quickly. Check the oil level once it has cooled, and call before driving on. Who handles it at Shine. All mechanical repairs, and logbook servicing to keep the oil changed on time. Red light: stop safely. Brake system. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. On most cars it lights up when the park brake is on. If it stays on with the park brake off, the brake fluid may be low or there may be a fault in the brakes. Can I keep driving? Check the park brake first. If the light stays on, stop somewhere safe and don't drive on until the brakes have been checked. Who handles it at Shine. All mechanical repairs (brakes). Amber light: get it checked soon. ABS. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. The anti-lock braking system has a fault. Your normal brakes should still work, but the wheels can lock under hard braking. Can I keep driving? Usually yes, carefully. Leave extra room in front and book it in soon. If the red brake light is on as well, stop safely. Who handles it at Shine. All mechanical repairs (brakes). Amber light: get it checked soon. Tyre pressure. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. One or more tyres is below its set pressure. Only cars with tyre pressure monitoring have this light. Can I keep driving? Gently, to the nearest air pump. Inflate the tyres to the pressures on the tyre placard, often inside the driver's door. If a tyre looks flat or the car pulls to one side, stop somewhere safe. Who handles it at Shine. Tyres. Red on many cars: don't put it off. Airbag (SRS). Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. The airbag system has found a fault. The airbags, and on some cars the seatbelt pretensioners, may not work in a crash. Can I keep driving? The car will usually drive normally, but you and your passengers are less protected. Have it checked soon. Who handles it at Shine. Call the workshop and describe what the light is doing. We'll tell you what to do next. Red light: stop safely. Engine temperature. Call (02) 8798 5715. What it usually means. The engine is running too hot. Common causes are low coolant, a leak, or a fault with the fan, thermostat or water pump. Can I keep driving? No. Stop as soon as it's safe and switch off. Let the engine cool, and never open the radiator cap while it's hot
